text: Testosterone is a steroidal hormone derived from cholesterol in the Leydig cells of the testes via the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, and small quantities are synthesized in the adrenals and ovaries (39). Men have an amount of circulating testosterone approximately 10-fold greater than women, and this hormonal discrepancy between the sexes is believed to be in large part responsible for the greater muscularity seen in postpubescent males (88). The overwhelming majority of circulating testosterone is bound to either sex hormone-binding globulin (60%) or albumin (38%); the residual amount of approximately 2% circulates in an unbound state.
